content.title: What happened between Dawn Staley, Geno Auriemma at end of South Carolina win vs UConn?
content.text: Updated April 3, 2026, 10:56 p.m. ETTensions appeared to boil over at the end of South Carolina women's basketball's Final Four win over UConn.The No. 1 seed Gamecocks (36-3) won 62-48 over No. 1 overall seed UConn (38-1) at Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix on April 3 to advance to the national championship game on April 5 (3:30 p.m. ET, ABC).With 0.8 seconds left in the game, UConn coach Geno Auriemma approached South Carolina coach Dawn Staley for the postgame handshake. However, the interaction quickly erupted into a verbal altercation, and assistant coaches had to step in to separate Staley and Auriemma."I have no idea (what went wrong on the sideline), but I'm going to let you know this. I'm of integrity," Staley told ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe in her postgame interview. "So if I did something wrong to Geno, I had no idea."Staley, confused about the incident, told Rowe she believed Auriemma's frustration stemmed from her not shaking hands with him before the game, which Staley said didn't happen."I guess he thought I didn't shake his hand at the beginning of the game. I don't know," Staley said. "I went down there pregame, shook everybody on his staff's hand. ... But hey, sometimes things get heated. We move on."The game's environment was already tense after Auriemma's comments about officiating earlier in the game. Before the start of the fourth quarter, he expressed his displeasure to Rowe about the officiating, claiming Staley had called the officials "names you don't want to hear."Despite the heated moment, Staley was clear she didn't want the sideline interaction to lessen her team's achievement. The Gamecocks are heading to the national championship for the third straight year. Staley is just the fourth coach ever to accomplish that feat."I'm super proud of our kids, and I'm not going to let any of this here take anything away from the performance on the floor," she said.What Dawn Staley, Geno Auriemma said about the altercationWhen asked about the interaction with Auriemma, Staley said at her press conference that Auriemma initiated the argument and that his reason for doing so was "a Geno question."Auriemma did not elaborate much on what sparked the heated conversation on his end or what he said to Staley when asked."I said what I said," Auriemma said. "And obviously she didn't like it. I just told the truth."He did confirm Staley's claim that he was frustrated she did not shake his hand pregame at center court."For 41 years, I've been coaching, and, I don't know, 25 Final Fours. The protocol is, before the game, you meet at halfcourt. Anybody see that before? Two coaches meet at halfcourt, and they shake hands, correct? ... They announce it on the loudspeaker. I waited there for like three minutes. So it is what it is."When a reporter pointed out that there was video of Staley shaking his hand and his assistant coaches' hands pregame, he told the reporter they'd "missed the point," and that he'd "rather not go into it."Tia Reid covers Jackson State sports for theClarion Ledger. Email her attreid@usatodayco.com and follow her on X @tiareid65.
